newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arison group registers for Hapoalim sale.
newsitem.headline: Arison group registers for Hapoalim sale.

text.p: A consortium headed by entrepreneur Ted Arison has formally registered to participate in the tender to acquire Israel's Bank Hapoalim, MI Holdings, the company selling the state-owned banks said on Tuesday.
The Arison group is one of two that are expected to enter the bidding for Israel's largest commercial bank. The deadline for submitting offers to participate in the sale is April 18.
The group made a deposit of $40 million, said Meir Jacobson, MI Holdings managing director.

Besides Arison, a U.S.-Israeli entrepreneur, the group includes Claridge Israel, an investment company controlled by Charles Bronfman; U.S. investor Michael Steinhardt and his partner Shlomo Topor; Israel's Dankner Group; Hyperion, a U.S. bank investment fund; and U.S. insurance entrepreneur Len Abramson, Jacobson said.
Steinhardt and Topor control Israel Maritime Bank, which they have been seeking to sell.

Jacobson said some of the partners already had permits from the Bank of Israel to control a bank. He said they would have to re-apply, as would the group as a whole, but predicted the approvals would come quickly.
Claridge had led an earlier bid for control of Hapoalim, but dropped out. In March, MI Holdings announced a new tender.

The Israeli government controls 78 percent of Hapoalim, with the remainder traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. It aims to sell between 25 percent and 69.3 percent through the tender, which it hopes to complete by mid-August.

The second group expected to submit its candidacy is led by Jeffrey Keil, a U.S. banker and is expected to include Eliezer Fishman, an Israeli entepreneur who sought to form a group to bid on Hapoalim in the previous round.
